claims.text: The governing distance is the trace. EV-GPS-00802 records trace_distance_km of 10.06 km against a booked optimal of 1.1 km on EV-TRIP-00802, an excess of 8.96 km — 814.5% of optimal and far past the 0.8 km absolute gate. Both limbs of the POL-RD-01 establishment test pass, so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own measurement.

POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing field and expressly forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test. Here the trace figure (10.06 km, EV-GPS-00802) and the trip_record copy (10.06 km, EV-TRIP-00802) agree, so there is no discrepancy to arbitrate and the excess is measured on the trace as the clause requires.

The trace is clean for policy purposes. EV-GPS-00802 carries 162 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 10 seconds — no gap over 90 seconds, no sustained interval above 30 seconds, and a sampling record with no discontinuity that could hide a straight-line jump over 500 m. The trace is therefore NOT impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), and the excess may be established on the trace without independent corroboration.

The deviation is additionally MATERIAL: the 8.96 km excess exceeds the 8.0 km absolute material threshold and the 814.5% excess exceeds the 50% material threshold, so the driver_profile check in POL-RD-06 is mandatory on this record.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. Under POL-RD-02, recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 1.1 + 0.28 x 4.0) x surge_multiplier 1.0, read from EV-FARE-00802) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 fixed surcharge + 0 waiting time - 0 promo = 6.545. Charged_total is 19.65, so the refund is 19.65 - 6.545 = 13.105, rounded up to 13.15; that is well above the 0.50 de minimis floor.

This is a METERED trip: fare_breakdown.fare_model on EV-FARE-00802 is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and the distance-and-time refund route under POL-RD-02 is open to the rider.

No rider-requested detour can excuse any part of the excess. POL-RD-04 requires an instruction recorded in the chat_log, and EV-CHAT-00802 contains zero messages (message_count 0, messages empty), so there is no instruction, no waypoint_hint and nothing to corroborate; the clause is unavailable and no distance may be excluded on that footing.

No traffic advisory covers this trip, so no external-cause exoneration is available. EV-ADVIS-00802-01 is MISSING: it has no payload and its admissibility weight_multiplier is 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — a point I disclose as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. Because no advisory record exists, POL-RD-03 cannot be run, the driver's side has no advisory to point to, and under POL-RD-13 the measured excess stands unadjusted.

No amendment to the endpoints was made. EV-TRIP-00802 shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min both null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and the booked 1.1 km optimal remains the correct baseline.

This is not a pooled trip. EV-TRIP-00802 records vehicle_type RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12 has no application and the matched-itinerary baseline it describes cannot displace the booked optimal of 1.1 km.

The rider has discharged the POL-RD-08 initial burden: the trip identifier TRP-00802 and the 14:00:00 pickup/start timestamp match across EV-TRIP-00802, EV-GPS-00802 and EV-FARE-00802, and the 8.96 km excess is measured from an unimpaired trace. The burden has therefore shifted to the driver, who on this record points to no specific artifact and no clause invoking POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12. The rider's own profile does not add a corroboration requirement, because deviation_claims_60d on EV-RPROF-00802 is 0 and the POL-RD-08 rider-profile condition needs 4 or more.

A repeat deviation pattern is established on the only fields POL-RD-06 permits. EV-DPROF-00802 records deviation_flags_90d of 3, which meets the clause's '3 or more' limb outright (it is also 3/200 of completed_trips_90d). I rely solely on deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d, as POL-RD-06 and POL-GEN-01 require; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only and is not used to ground anything.

Because the deviation is both MATERIAL on this trip's trace and substantiated on this trip's own evidence, POL-RD-06(b) licenses FULL_REFUND of the charged total of 19.65 rather than the POL-RD-02 partial, and I state the two figures side by side as the clause demands: the POL-RD-02 figure is 13.15, the uplifted figure is 19.65. No government-set or third-party pass-through line is uplifted or excluded, because EV-FARE-00802 carries no ERP, toll or airport surcharge line at all. The finding of deviation itself rests on POL-RD-01 evidence for this trip alone, not on the pattern.

A conduct referral follows from the same finding. POL-RD-06(c) requires the case to be added to driver-conduct review, and under POL-GEN-03 a referral adds to the ruling rather than replacing it: it does not delay and does not suppress the monetary outcome.

Nothing in EV-FARE-00802 supports a pass-through correction, and nothing may be double-counted. The fare carries no ERP gantry charge (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00, off-optimal-route ERP total 0.00) and no airport surcharge (airport_surcharge 0.00) on a trip that does not originate at an airport; the rider's entire loss is the 19.65 charged total already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 and POL-RD-06(b) figures, so no separate POL-RD-09 addition arises.

The rider presently carries the whole charge, so the outcome that makes the rider whole is a refund and not NO_ACTION. EV-FARE-00802 shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0; under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION would leave that charge standing against the filing rider, whereas the arithmetic above returns money to the rider.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires, and this case must end in a monetary ruling rather than terminal escalation. The identifiers all match TRP-00802, the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), no exculpatory clause is invoked against any missing artifact, no timestamps conflict, and the refund (13.15, or 19.65 uplifted) is below both the 150.00 ceiling and the charged_total ceiling. Every charge line on EV-FARE-00802 - base fare, distance, time, platform fee - has a counterpart in the trip record and trace.

claims.text: The rider has claimed the whole fare, but on this METERED fare the record fixes the refund arithmetically and it is not the whole fare: the recomputed optimal-route fare is ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 1.1 km + 0.28 x 4.0 min) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 6.5450, and the refund is the charged total of SGD 19.65 less SGD 6.5450 = SGD 13.105, rounded up to SGD 13.15. The driver retains SGD 6.5450 for a trip that was in fact driven, and the contested amount of SGD 19.65 is overstated by SGD 6.50.

The refund of SGD 13.15 is 66.7% of the SGD 19.65 charged, which is below the 90% threshold POL-RD-02 sets for a full refund, so the outcome on the policy's own arithmetic is a PARTIAL_REFUND of the contested amount and nothing more; the fare record's own reaches_full_refund_share flag is false and its refund quantum is SGD 0.05.

Nothing may be added on top of that SGD 13.15 figure as a pass-through correction. This fare carries no ERP charges at all (the on-optimal-route total and the off-optimal-route total are both SGD 0.00, with no gantry lines), no airport surcharge, no waiting-time fee and no surge uplift, and under POL-RD-09(1) any off-route ERP would in any event already be comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund and must never be added a second time.

There is no billing-integrity correction available to the rider under POL-RD-09(4). Every line on this fare has a counterpart in the trip: the distance billed (10.06 km) is the trace's own length, the time billed (26.8 min) is the recorded trip duration, the base fare and platform fee are the rate-card constants, and there is no gantry line and no airport surcharge anywhere on the fare. No phantom line exists, so there is nothing to refund as a standalone correction beyond the recomputation.

The POL-RD-06(b) uplift to a full refund of the charged total should not be applied on this record. That limb licenses the uplift only for a deviation that is 'substantiated on this trip's own evidence', and beyond the trace there is nothing here: the chat log carries no messages at all (0 message count, no first or last message), no counterparty statement is on file, no ERP gantry line places the vehicle on any corridor, and the billed distance is the trace figure itself - which POL-RD-07(ii) treats as non-independent corroboration precisely because the meter is derived from the same trace. The two limbs of POL-RD-06 are drafted differently on purpose - limb (a) requires support from 'at least one artifact other than the gps_trace', limb (b) requires the deviation to be substantiated - and a trace-only file should be left at the POL-RD-02 figure of SGD 13.15.

If the driver-profile check in POL-RD-06 is run at all, it should be run at the floor of the clause's range and with only the two counters the clause names. The only citable fields are deviation_flags_90d (3) and completed_trips_90d (200), a rate of 1.5% - less than a third of the 5% ratio limb - with the bare count of 3 sitting exactly at the clause's stated minimum. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 asks for and may not be substituted for it under POL-GEN-01; it is context only.

The driver does not resist the POL-RD-01 finding on this trip's own trace, which is complete and unimpaired for policy purposes - 100% coverage, no gaps, a 10-second sampling interval against a 10-second expected interval, and a maximum gap of 10 seconds - and records 10.06 km against a booked optimal of 1.1 km, an excess of 8.96 km (814.5%) that clears both establishment tests and both materiality tests. The driver's case is therefore about quantum, not liability, and the quantum the policy computes is SGD 13.15.

No traffic advisory is on file for this trip, and the driver says so rather than stretching the record: EV-ADVIS-00802-01 is MISSING, it carries weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and it has no payload, while the trace's own advisory-area block returns an empty advisory list. The driver therefore advances no external-cause exoneration and no amended optimal under POL-RD-03 and confines this brief to the remedy; under POL-GEN-02(1) and (3) the impairment of that artifact is disclosed here, and its absence is a gap in the bundle, not an exculpatory finding for either party.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: I find the route deviation established on this trip's own evidence and I order the whole contested fare of SGD 19.65 returned to the rider. The driver's argument for a partial refund of SGD 13.15 is rejected because POL-RD-06(b) applies on this record.

Liability. EV-GPS-00802 records trace_distance_km of 10.06 km against the booked optimal 1.1 km on EV-TRIP-00802. The excess is 8.96 km, or 814.5% of optimal. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%) and both materiality thresholds (more than 8.0 km and more than 50%). The trace is clean for POL-RD-07: 162 fixes, a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage and no gap over 90 seconds. It is therefore not impaired, no independent corroboration is needed, and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises.

Fare arithmetic. The POL-RD-02 recomputation is: charged_total SGD 19.65; recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 1.1 km + 0.28 x 4.0 min) x 1.0 surge read from EV-FARE-00802) + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 6.5450; POL-RD-02 refund = 19.65 - 6.5450 = SGD 13.105, rounded up to SGD 13.15. That is the figure the driver asks for, and it is correct as the POL-RD-02 partial figure.

POL-RD-06 uplift. The deviation is material, so the driver-profile check is mandatory. Using only the citable fields, EV-DPROF-00802 shows deviation_flags_90d = 3 and completed_trips_90d = 200. POL-RD-06's first limb is met at '3 or more', so a repeat pattern is established; the 1.5% ratio does not matter because the count limb is independently satisfied. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only and is not used. Because the deviation is both material and substantiated on this trip's own evidence, POL-RD-06(b) uplifts the remedy to FULL_REFUND of the charged total. I state the two figures side by side as required: the POL-RD-02 figure is SGD 13.15; the uplifted figure is SGD 19.65. EV-FARE-00802 carries no ERP, toll, airport surcharge or other government-set or third-party pass-through line, so nothing is carved out of the full refund. The driver's argument that the trace alone cannot substantiate the deviation is rejected: POL-RD-07(ii) imposes an independent-corroboration requirement only when the trace is impaired, and this trace is not impaired.

Other issues. EV-CHAT-00802 has zero messages, so POL-RD-04 cannot apply. EV-TRIP-00802 shows no endpoint amendment and vehicle_type RYDE_X, so POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 do not apply. EV-ADVIS-00802-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT; no party relies on it as an external-cause exoneration, and its absence does not trigger POL-RD-10(5) here. No billing-integrity defect appears on EV-FARE-00802, so no POL-RD-09(4) referral is made. The identifiers match, no timestamps conflict, and no POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires.

Confidence and execution. The relied-on artifacts carry weight 1.0. The missing advisory carries 0.0 but does not carry the deciding fact. Confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 floor. Because the monetary effect of SGD 19.65 exceeds the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, this provisional ruling is issued but the amount is held for human release under POL-GEN-05. The POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral does not delay or displace the refund.
referrals: POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct review for a material, substantiated deviation with an established repeat pattern (driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d = 3).

ruling.explanation:
The route deviation is established on this trip's own evidence, and POL-RD-06(b) uplifts the remedy to a full refund of the SGD 19.65 charged. Reasons below.

Deviation (POL-RD-01). EV-GPS-00802 records trace_distance_km of 10.06 km against the booked optimal of 1.1 km on EV-TRIP-00802 — an excess of 8.96 km, 814.5% of optimal, clearing both the 20% and 0.8 km establishment gates and both the 50% and 8.0 km materiality gates. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 162 fixes, a 10-second sampling interval against a 10-second expected interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 10 seconds, so no POL-RD-07(a)-(c) impairment applies and the excess stands on the trace without independent corroboration. Both advocates agree on this finding and I accept it.

Fare arithmetic (POL-RD-02), stated on separate lines as the clause requires. charged_total on EV-FARE-00802 = SGD 19.65. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 1.1 km + 0.28 x 4.0 min) x 1.0 surge, read from EV-FARE-00802) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 fixed surcharge + 0 waiting time - 0 promo = SGD 6.5450. The POL-RD-02 refund = 19.65 - 6.5450 = SGD 13.105, rounded up to SGD 13.15 — above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, and 66.9% of charged_total, below the 90% share at which POL-RD-02 alone would give a full refund.

Driver-profile uplift (POL-RD-06). The deviation is MATERIAL, so the driver-profile check is mandatory. On the only two citable fields — deviation_flags_90d = 3 and completed_trips_90d = 200 on EV-DPROF-00802 — the count limb of the pattern test is met (3 or more); the ratio limb is not (3/200 = 1.5%, below 5%), but the count limb alone establishes the pattern. I have used no other profile field. The rider's and driver's mentions of prior_deviation_flags are correct that it is context only under POL-GEN-01, and neither side grounds a finding on it.

The driver's advocate argues POL-RD-06(b) should not fire because nothing corroborates the trace — the chat log has zero messages, there is no counterparty statement, no ERP gantry line, and the billed distance is a copy of the trace. I reject that. Limb (b) requires a deviation that is MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own evidence. The trace is this trip's own evidence, it is unimpaired, and it shows the deviation; the clause's own note confirms the finding is POL-RD-01 on this trip's trace. The independent-corroboration requirement the driver relies on comes from POL-RD-07(ii), which governs only where the trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c); it is not impaired here, so that requirement does not apply. Limb (b) therefore fires. The driver's residual point — that the refund is not the whole fare under POL-RD-02 alone — is correct as far as it goes and is reflected in the SGD 13.15 figure above; the uplift is what takes the remedy to SGD 19.65.

Remedy, with both figures printed side by side as POL-RD-06(b) demands: the POL-RD-02 figure is SGD 13.15; the uplifted figure is the charged total of SGD 19.65. The uplift reaches the whole charge because EV-FARE-00802 carries no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge line (all zero) for POL-RD-09 to settle separately. I rule FULL_REFUND of SGD 19.65 to the rider.

Remaining claims. Both advocates' POL-RD-09 points are accepted: there is no ERP, no airport surcharge on a trip that does not originate at an airport, no waiting-time fee and no surge uplift, so no standalone pass-through correction arises and nothing may be added on top of the recomputed figure (POL-RD-09(1)); nor is there any phantom line for POL-RD-09(4). The absence of a rider-requested detour is accepted — EV-CHAT-00802 has zero messages, so POL-RD-04 has no instruction, no waypoint_hint and nothing to corroborate — and the absence of any endpoint amendment is accepted (both amendment timestamps and both amended-optimal fields are null on EV-TRIP-00802), so POL-RD-05 does not run. The trip is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. The fare is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 runs. EV-ADVIS-00802-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), no party advances an external traffic excuse, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable and no closure-adjusted optimal is on the record.

No POL-RD-10 escalation fires: the trip identifiers all match TRP-00802, the trace is unimpaired, no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact, no timestamps conflict, the refund is below both SGD 150.00 and charged_total, and every fare line (base, distance, time, platform fee) has a counterpart in the trip record and trace.

ruling.explanation:
Addressed to both parties. This ruling is made on the record of trip TRP-00802.

1. The deviation is established on this trip's own measurement. GPS trace EV-GPS-00802 runs 10.06 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff; the booked optimal route on EV-TRIP-00802 is 1.1 km. The excess is 8.96 km, 814.5% of optimal — past both establishment gates (20% and 0.8 km) and both materiality gates (50% and 8.0 km). POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure governing, and the trip record's copy (10.06 km) agrees, so there is no discrepancy to arbitrate. Both advocates accept this and I accept it.

3. The fare. That is 66.9% of the charge, below the 90% share at which POL-RD-02 alone would give a full refund, so on POL-RD-02 alone the outcome would be a partial refund of SGD 13.15.

4. Why the ruling is nevertheless a full refund. POL-RD-01 records a material deviation, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is mandatory. On the only two fields the clause permits (POL-GEN-01), driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 3 against completed_trips_90d of 200: the bare count meets the clause's '3 or more' limb, so a repeat pattern is established. The deviation is also material and substantiated on this trip's own evidence — the unimpaired trace, the booked optimal and the fare statement. I reject the driver advocate's contention that limb (b) additionally requires corroboration beyond the trace, and that the billed distance cannot serve because it is derived from the same trace: that non-independence rule is imposed by POL-RD-07(ii) only where the trace is impaired, and this trace is not impaired, so the deviation may be established on it alone. The clause's own note confirms the finding is 'POL-RD-01 on this trip's trace'. The deterrent uplift therefore replaces the partial figure. Stating both as the clause requires: the POL-RD-02 figure is SGD 13.15; the uplifted figure is SGD 19.65, the whole charged total. There are no government-set or third-party pass-through lines to carve out — the fare's ERP, toll and airport-surcharge lines are all zero and the trip does not originate at an airport.

5. The driver's remaining quantum points are accepted. His contention that the 66.9% share caps the outcome at a partial refund is rejected for the reason in paragraph 4.

6. The traffic advisory. EV-ADVIS-00802-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; its absence is disclosed by both briefs and is itself citable. Neither party asserts an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 is not invoked against that artifact and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged; no exoneration and no amended optimal arise, and the measured excess stands unadjusted (POL-RD-13). No chat instruction exists (the chat log is empty), so POL-RD-04 excludes nothing; no endpoint was amended, so POL-RD-05 does not apply; the trip is RYDE_X, not pooled, so POL-RD-12 does not apply.

7. Referral. Because a repeat pattern is established alongside a material deviation, POL-RD-06(c) requires the case to be referred to driver-conduct review. The referral rides with the money and neither delays nor displaces it. No POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral arises, as no charge line is unmatched.

8. Amount, execution and the parties' positions. The refund is SGD 19.65 — the whole contested amount, returned to the filing rider; payment status on EV-FARE-00802 is CHARGED with 0.00 refunded, so this returns money rather than leaving the charge standing (POL-GEN-03). No driver compensation arises: the rider was billed for the full traced distance and no unbilled-distance shortfall exists under POL-RD-04. The monetary effect of SGD 19.65 exceeds the SGD 8.00 execution threshold in POL-GEN-05, so the ruling issues but is not executed automatically — the amount is held and the case enters the queue for release by a human reviewer.

9. Confidence. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts — EV-GPS-00802, EV-TRIP-00802 and EV-FARE-00802 — is at weight 1.0, so the cap on confidence is 1.0; I set it at 0.90. This is a provisional ruling made without human review and may be appealed within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

ledger.claim: Because the deviation is both MATERIAL on this trip's trace and substantiated on this trip's own evidence, POL-RD-06(b) licenses FULL_REFUND of the charged total of 19.65 rather than the POL-RD-02 partial, and I state the two figures side by side as the clause demands: the POL-RD-02 figure is 13.15, the uplifted figure is 19.65. No government-set or third-party pass-through line is uplifted or excluded, because EV-FARE-00802 carries no ERP, toll or airport surcharge line at all. The finding of deviation itself rests on POL-RD-01 evidence for this trip alone, not on the pattern.

A conduct referral follows from the same finding. POL-RD-06(c) requires the case to be added to driver-conduct review, and under POL-GEN-03 a referral adds to the ruling rather than replacing it: it does not delay and does not suppress the monetary outcome.

Nothing in EV-FARE-00802 supports a pass-through correction, and nothing may be double-counted. The fare carries no ERP gantry charge (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00, off-optimal-route ERP total 0.00) and no airport surcharge (airport_surcharge 0.00) on a trip that does not originate at an airport; the rider's entire loss is the 19.65 charged total already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 and POL-RD-06(b) figures, so no separate POL-RD-09 addition arises.

The rider presently carries the whole charge, so the outcome that makes the rider whole is a refund and not NO_ACTION. EV-FARE-00802 shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0; under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION would leave that charge standing against the filing rider, whereas the arithmetic above returns money to the rider.

No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires, and this case must end in a monetary ruling rather than terminal escalation. The identifiers all match TRP-00802, the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), no exculpatory clause is invoked against any missing artifact, no timestamps conflict, and the refund (13.15, or 19.65 uplifted) is below both the 150.00 ceiling and the charged_total ceiling. Every charge line on EV-FARE-00802 - base fare, distance, time, platform fee - has a counterpart in the trip record and trace.

The rider has claimed the whole fare, but on this METERED fare the record fixes the refund arithmetically and it is not the whole fare: the recomputed optimal-route fare is ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 1.1 km + 0.28 x 4.0 min) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 6.5450, and the refund is the charged total of SGD 19.65 less SGD 6.5450 = SGD 13.105, rounded up to SGD 13.15. The driver retains SGD 6.5450 for a trip that was in fact driven, and the contested amount of SGD 19.65 is overstated by SGD 6.50.

The refund of SGD 13.15 is 66.7% of the SGD 19.65 charged, which is below the 90% threshold POL-RD-02 sets for a full refund, so the outcome on the policy's own arithmetic is a PARTIAL_REFUND of the contested amount and nothing more; the fare record's own reaches_full_refund_share flag is false and its refund quantum is SGD 0.05.

Nothing may be added on top of that SGD 13.15 figure as a pass-through correction. This fare carries no ERP charges at all (the on-optimal-route total and the off-optimal-route total are both SGD 0.00, with no gantry lines), no airport surcharge, no waiting-time fee and no surge uplift, and under POL-RD-09(1) any off-route ERP would in any event already be comprehended in the POL-RD-02 refund and must never be added a second time.

There is no billing-integrity correction available to the rider under POL-RD-09(4). Every line on this fare has a counterpart in the trip: the distance billed (10.06 km) is the trace's own length, the time billed (26.8 min) is the recorded trip duration, the base fare and platform fee are the rate-card constants, and there is no gantry line and no airport surcharge anywhere on the fare. No phantom line exists, so there is nothing to refund as a standalone correction beyond the recomputation.

The POL-RD-06(b) uplift to a full refund of the charged total should not be applied on this record. That limb licenses the uplift only for a deviation that is 'substantiated on this trip's own evidence', and beyond the trace there is nothing here: the chat log carries no messages at all (0 message count, no first or last message), no counterparty statement is on file, no ERP gantry line places the vehicle on any corridor, and the billed distance is the trace figure itself - which POL-RD-07(ii) treats as non-independent corroboration precisely because the meter is derived from the same trace. The two limbs of POL-RD-06 are drafted differently on purpose - limb (a) requires support from 'at least one artifact other than the gps_trace', limb (b) requires the deviation to be substantiated - and a trace-only file should be left at the POL-RD-02 figure of SGD 13.15.

If the driver-profile check in POL-RD-06 is run at all, it should be run at the floor of the clause's range and with only the two counters the clause names. The only citable fields are deviation_flags_90d (3) and completed_trips_90d (200), a rate of 1.5% - less than a third of the 5% ratio limb - with the bare count of 3 sitting exactly at the clause's stated minimum. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 asks for and may not be substituted for it under POL-GEN-01; it is context only.

ledger.claim: The driver does not resist the POL-RD-01 finding on this trip's own trace, which is complete and unimpaired for policy purposes - 100% coverage, no gaps, a 10-second sampling interval against a 10-second expected interval, and a maximum gap of 10 seconds - and records 10.06 km against a booked optimal of 1.1 km, an excess of 8.96 km (814.5%) that clears both establishment tests and both materiality tests. The driver's case is therefore about quantum, not liability, and the quantum the policy computes is SGD 13.15.

No traffic advisory is on file for this trip, and the driver says so rather than stretching the record: EV-ADVIS-00802-01 is MISSING, it carries weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and it has no payload, while the trace's own advisory-area block returns an empty advisory list.
